from itertools import permutations

# Category inference from the adjective meanings in the question.
groups = {
    "opinion": "good lovely silly wonderful awful nice ridiculous terrible",
    "purpose": "drinking snorkeling typing exercise eating whittling smoking hiking driving",
    "size": "massive big enormous huge midsize normal-size small large medium-size tiny little",
    "color": "gray yellow maroon violet green indigo black teal cyan crimson blue pink brown aqua",
    "age": "archaic ancient old-fashioned brand-new old new",
    "shape": "spherical square circular pyramidal rectangular prismlike triangular",
    "material": "glass steel iron wool plastic rubber fiberglass wood paper",
    "origin": "vietnamese turkish russian thai bangladeshi iranian ethiopian indian mexican filipino american japanese",
}
category = {
    word: name
    for name, words in groups.items()
    for word in words.split()
}

# All examples containing multiple adjectives. Single-adjective examples
# impose no relative-order constraints.
observations = {
    9: "good gray archaic",
    19: "massive yellow",
    21: "good drinking",
    23: "big maroon",
    26: "enormous violet",
    29: "glass vietnamese",
    30: "lovely snorkeling",
    31: "ancient spherical",
    33: "old-fashioned spherical",
    35: "brand-new square",
    38: "good typing",
    40: "silly exercise",
    44: "steel turkish",
    45: "iron russian",
    47: "silly snorkeling",
    48: "huge green",
    52: "silly eating",
    54: "steel thai",
    58: "brand-new circular",
    59: "brand-new pyramidal",
    62: "huge indigo",
    64: "midsize black",
    67: "wonderful whittling",
    69: "steel bangladeshi",
    77: "wool iranian",
    79: "ancient rectangular",
    80: "plastic thai",
    82: "big black",
    83: "rubber russian",
    86: "iron ethiopian",
    89: "normal-size teal",
    91: "ridiculous typing",
    92: "small cyan",
    94: "huge yellow",
    95: "awful whittling",
    97: "old prismlike",
    98: "silly whittling",
    103: "terrible smoking",
    108: "huge crimson",
    109: "old-fashioned pyramidal",
    110: "old triangular",
    116: "ancient spherical",
    117: "nice snorkeling",
    119: "big maroon",
    125: "ancient circular",
    127: "driving midsize rectangular",
    130: "steel russian",
    132: "terrible hiking",
    135: "large crimson",
    140: "brand-new spherical",
    142: "fiberglass indian",
    144: "normal-size maroon",
}

options = {
    "A": "nice typing big yellow new rectangular wool",
    "B": "silly whittling little gray archaic square vietnamese",
    "C": "mexican medium-size violet ancient spherical typing silly",
    "D": "plastic large blue old-fashioned rectangular whittling good",
    "E": "wood turkish tiny pink archaic prismlike whittling",
    "F": "silly hiking medium-size black old-fashioned spherical mexican steel",
    "G": "terrible eating midsize green brand-new prismlike",
    "H": "filipino paper small violet new spherical snorkeling",
    "I": "snorkeling little brown old circular plastic american",
    "J": "japanese glass midsize aqua brand-new spherical",
}

edges = set()
for phrase in observations.values():
    cats = [category[word] for word in phrase.split()]
    for i in range(len(cats)):
        for j in range(i + 1, len(cats)):
            edges.add((cats[i], cats[j]))

# Exhaustively enumerate all category orders consistent with every example.
orders = []
for order in permutations(groups):
    rank = {name: i for i, name in enumerate(order)}
    if all(rank[a] < rank[b] for a, b in edges):
        orders.append(rank)

if not orders:
    print("Examples admit no consistent category order.")
    print("CHECK UNKNOWN")
else:
    counts = {}
    for letter, phrase in options.items():
        cats = [category[word] for word in phrase.split()]
        counts[letter] = sum(
            all(rank[a] < rank[b] for a, b in zip(cats, cats[1:]))
            for rank in orders
        )

    print("Exhaustively checked category orders:", len(orders))
    for letter, count in counts.items():
        print(f"{letter}: correct in {count}/{len(orders)} consistent orders")

    possible = "".join(k for k, n in counts.items() if n)
    forced = "".join(k for k, n in counts.items() if n == len(orders))
    print("Compatible choices:", possible or "K")
    print("Choices correct under every consistent order:", forced or "(none)")

    # To refute K, one universally correct option is sufficient.
    if forced:
        print("Submitted answer: K")
        print("K is false: at least option " + forced[0] +
              " has the required order under every consistent category order.")
        print("CHECK FAIL")
    elif not possible:
        print("CHECK PASS")
    else:
        print("UNSUPPORTED: the examples do not determine whether K is correct.")
        print("CHECK UNKNOWN")
